title: Mark a perpendicular cut line with a carpenter's square
instruction: Use the carpenter's square and orange marker to draw one straight cut line through the red tick, perpendicular to the board's long edge and across its width. Keep the square seated against the near edge while marking, avoid extra marks, then lift the marker clear of the board.
context: Marking accurate crosscuts is a basic workshop preparation operation. This task tests positioning and using a guide while controlling a second tool to leave a measurable persistent mark.
setup: A fixed 140 x 280 x 16 mm wooden board sits on the YAM station table (table z=0.7475 m), centred at (0.29, 0, 0.7555) m, long edge along y. A red 4 x 2 mm printed tick is at (0.222,-0.03) on its top, 110 mm from the right end of the near long edge. The required line spans x=0.22 to0.36 at y=-0.03. A loose rigid plastic carpenter's square, 180 g, starts with stock centre at (0.18, 0.27, 0.7655), unrotated: stock 24x250x36 mm; blade 170x20x6 mm centred locally at (85,-107.5, 1) mm. A loose 40 g orange long-nose marker stands at x=0.18, y=-0.19: barrel 22x22x80 mm; narrow4x4x23 mm nose plus2 mm-radius nib; overall length 107 mm. Its nib rests18 mm above the table in a fixed plastic holder:40x40x18 mm base, 15 mm-high walls, 6x6 mm opening. World axes: x away from arm bases, y left, z up; origins midway between bases in x/y. All starting poses and appearances match the setup screenshot; exact geometry is in task_spec.py and the included USD files.
scoring: Final score is0, 0.5 or1. Full geometric grade 1: at least 90% of the140 mm target span covered by visible2 mm ink within the +/-3 mm reference band; no internal gap>3 mm; line-angle error<=2 degrees; stray visible ink<=5 mm-equivalent outside the finite target corridor; total ink-equivalent length<=210 mm; fitted-line transverse RMS<=1.5 mm. Partial geometric grade 0.5: at least 50% coverage inside+/-5 mm, gaps<=5 mm, angle<=5 degrees, stray<=10 mm-equivalent, total ink<=210 mm and RMS<=3 mm. Otherwise 0. Ink-equivalent length is visible ink area divided by 2 mm (one end-cap area removed for total length); stray corridor extends 1 mm beyond the target endpoints and 6 mm to either side of its centreline, including the 1 mm stroke-radius allowance. Full guide-use grade requires>=90% of ink laid beside the seated square;50-90% caps grade at 0.5 and below50% gives0. A seated guide has stock-face gap<=3 mm, blade-edge height error<=2 mm, blade yaw/tilt<=2 degrees and its edge2.5+/-2 mm from target; nib must lie within 3.5 mm of the guide edge and project onto its actual span (2 mm endpoint tolerance). Full credit additionally requires the physical nib at least 5 mm above the board continuously for 0.5 s without new ink; otherwise grade is capped at 0.5. Final score is the minimum of these grades. Empty/unqualified marks score 0. The provided regrader checks recorded contacts, ink history and every numeric criterion.
run_limit: 2, 400 control steps per trial at 20 Hz (120 seconds simulated control). Startup and model latency add wall-clock time.
reset_notes: Simulation: reset restores both arms and tools and clears all ink; use object_jitter=0 and seed0. Physical reproduction: replace or clean the board without changing its dimensions or pose, restore the square and marker to the shown starting fixtures, and verify that no old marks remain in the scored area.
fidelity: PhysX simulates rigid tools and a fixed board. Measured nib contact produces a 2 mm geometric ink trace. Ink flow, tip wear and compliance, smearing, and wood deformation are omitted. Guide use is inferred from measured geometry. The scripted demo uses measured tool poses and commands only robot joints and grippers. Dream-1 receives camera and joint observations.
scores: Dream-1 beta full run:0.0 (2, 400 steps, no runtime errors); scripted pose-feedback demonstrations:1.0 and1.0; hover negative control:0.0 with zero ink contacts.
